_about: Real, sourced context for a HYPOTHETICAL scenario: a large AI data-centre campus in Seine-Saint-Denis. Everything under 'site', 'facts' and 'hypothetical' is invented for the simulation (plausible, based on the cited comparables). Everything under 'context' and 'realProjects' is real and sourced.
label: HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO — not a real project

site.label: Hypothetical site — Rateau industrial zone, La Courneuve
site.placeFr: dans la zone industrielle Rateau, à La Courneuve
rationale: Existing industrial land (OSM landuse=industrial, 'Zone Industrielle Rateau', way 47028132, about 28 ha), which fits the regional rule (SDRIF-E OR 126) that data centres go first to existing business sites.
Next to Europe's densest data-centre cluster (Plaine Commune / La Courneuve), with fibre and 225 kV substations nearby, so it is the kind of place a real developer would look at.

Close to dense housing, schools and the A86 motorway, so the consultation questions (noise, heat, generators, grid works, jobs, district heating) are realistic and touch different groups of residents.
Inside the map bbox and about 4 km from the Stade de France landmark, so it is visible on the map.
caveats: Indicative point only: no parcel-level study was done; the zone today hosts warehouses, municipal and road-authority depots and active industry (e.g. a Safran Electronics & Defense building a few hundred metres away in OSM).
This is NOT a real project. Real projects nearby (Paris Digital Park in La Courneuve, Dugny Digital Hub, the Segro project in Le Bourget) are listed in 'realProjects' and are separate.

hypothetical.proposalFr: PROJET HYPOTHÉTIQUE — avis de concertation préalable (exercice de simulation). Un opérateur propose de construire un campus de calcul pour l'intelligence artificielle dans la zone industrielle Rateau, à La Courneuve. Le site d'environ 8 hectares, aujourd'hui occupé par des entrepôts et ateliers, accueillerait trois bâtiments de 28 m de haut au maximum, pour une puissance électrique de 200 mégawatts. Le chantier durerait environ quatre ans, en trois phases, avec un poste électrique sur le site et deux lignes souterraines de 225 000 volts creusées sous la voirie jusqu'aux postes voisins. Le refroidissement fonctionnerait en circuit fermé (environ 5 000 m³ d'eau par an). Une centaine de groupes électrogènes de secours seraient testés chaque mois. L'opérateur s'engagerait à livrer jusqu'à 15 MW de chaleur au réseau de chauffage urbain, soit l'équivalent d'environ 5 000 logements. Il annonce environ 600 emplois au pic du chantier et 120 emplois permanents sur le site. Les recettes fiscales locales sont estimées entre 6 et 9 millions d'euros par an. Votre avis est sollicité.
hypothetical.proposalEn: HYPOTHETICAL PROJECT — notice of prior public consultation (simulation exercise). An operator proposes to build an artificial-intelligence computing campus in the Rateau industrial zone in La Courneuve. The site of about 8 hectares, now used by warehouses and workshops, would host three buildings up to 28 m high, drawing 200 megawatts of electricity. Construction would take about four years in three phases, with an on-site substation and two underground 225,000-volt lines dug under the streets to nearby substations. Cooling would run in a closed loop (about 5,000 m³ of water a year). Around a hundred backup generators would be tested every month. The operator would commit to supply up to 15 MW of heat to the district-heating network, roughly the needs of 5,000 homes. It announces about 600 jobs at the peak of construction and 120 permanent jobs on site. Local tax revenue is estimated at 6 to 9 million euros a year. Your opinion is invited.

concentration.fact: Île-de-France hosts 44 % of the 322 data centres counted in France at 31 Dec 2024, and about 65-70 % of installed power.

sources.name: Région Île-de-France — Stratégie régionale d'implantation des centres de données, rapport CR 2026-039 (juin 2026, PDF)

concentration.fact: Seine-Saint-Denis data centres consumed 0.8 TWh of electricity in 2024 — the highest of any French département (Seine-et-Marne and Hauts-de-Seine 0.3 TWh each).
concentration.caveat: Enedis figure; very large sites connected directly to RTE may not be fully included.

participationProcedure.summary: A large data-centre campus in France typically goes through: (1) possible CNDP public debate or prior consultation, (2) an environmental assessment with an opinion of the environmental authority (Ae/IGEDD or MRAe), (3) an environmental authorisation (classified installation: generators, refrigerants) with a public consultation run by a commissaire enquêteur, (4) a building permit, and in Île-de-France (5) a prior State approval for large business premises (urban-planning code L.510-1).

steps.detail: Industrial facilities whose buildings and infrastructure cost more than €300 M must be referred to the CNDP, which decides between a public debate (3-6 months) and a prior consultation with a guarantor; €150-300 M: publicity and optional referral (Code de l'environnement R.121-2 thresholds as described in parliamentary answers). Equipment (e.g. servers) does not count towards the cost. 2025-2026 simplification laws targeted the CNDP's scope — check the current text on Légifrance.
Ae (IGEDD) for Dugny (2024-08), MRAe Île-de-France for Le Bourget (APJIF-2025-056). Not for or against the project; the developer must answer it in writing before the public consultation.

sources.name: Autorité environnementale (IGEDD) — avis n° 2024-08 du 11 avril 2024, Dugny Digital Hub (PDF)
MRAe Île-de-France — avis APJIF-2025-056 du 30 juin 2025, centre de données au Bourget (PDF)

steps.detail: Since the 'industrie verte' law (no. 2023-973, 23 Oct 2023) and decree no. 2024-742 (6 Jul 2024), the public consultation for an environmental authorisation runs in parallel with the review (Code de l'environnement L.181-10-1), led by a commissaire enquêteur. Le Bourget: inquiry Oct-Nov 2025 then a supplementary consultation until Jan 2026 (press).

Since law no. 2026-403 of 26 May 2026 (art. 35), a data centre can be declared a 'projet d'intérêt national majeur' by decree: the prefect then issues the building permit and local height rules can be set aside; a permit can be refused for water stress; the energy minister can ask RTE to reserve grid capacity.

sources.name: Cabinet Gossement Avocats — Data centers: ce que change la loi n° 2026-403 du 26 mai 2026 (commentary)

steps.detail: SDRIF-E (approved 10 Jun 2025) OR 126: data centres first on existing business sites, limit environmental impacts, account for local grid capacity, recover waste heat, fit into the urban landscape.

sources.name: Région Île-de-France — Stratégie régionale d'implantation des centres de données, rapport CR 2026-039 (juin 2026, PDF)
